hum just curious, why you say cheerio is outdated? The last [cheerio release](https://github.com/cheeriojs/cheerio/releases) was shipped in less than one month ago.

I agree with "cheerio is bloated" but also it is the consequence when you need to support a lot of edge cases.

I can't feel too confident with node-html-parser; don't misunderstand me I'm sure it's a good project but I can't feel confident with it in the long term 🤔

No problem just thought I would help since it was easy. Cheerio on npm was published a year ago. Take a look at node-html-parser on npm and github, it's quite popular and old as well. It's a fork of original fast-html-parser. Cheerio might be more appropriate on larger projects but simple like this one is overkill. I would in fact prefer regex over any parser since it's parsing from fixed location.

I decided to keep cheerio, mostly because I use this library in combination with [metascraper](https://metascraper.js.org/) and since cheerio is already a metacraper dependency, cheerio is deduped and a not big deal in terms of disk space.

BTW, thanks for creating `hooman`! I have pending add it to [html-get](https://github.com/microlinkhq/html-get) 🙂

Useragents.me doesn't look so accurate. It says Mac OS X, Safari is the "Most Common Desktop Useragent" with 31.5 share and Windows Chrome is second with 17.34 share. That's very unlikely.

Edit: You can ignore everything below. [useragents.me](https://www.useragents.me/) intermittently cuts off the last character of the UA string so the entire site is worthless.

---

<details><summary>everything</summary>

There are several oddities with [useragents.me](https://www.useragents.me/). Specifically the "Most Common Desktop Useragents" list.

1. (Already mentioned above) Safari is severely overrepresented. In previous data here it almost always appeared after each combination of Windows/Mac/Linux + Chrome/Firefox. And Windows + Chrome was always the undefeated king.
2. The same for Mac OS being overrepresented compared to Windows.
3. For some reason Firefox isn't even recognized with it being listed as Other like it never came up when the site was written when it should be more popular than Safari even on Mac OS.
4. The list has weird gaps in it. Firefox again stands out the most with `Firefox/117` & `Firefox/115` somehow still making the list when `Firefox/119` (latest -1) doesn't.

Something is going wrong in that list. [useragents.me](https://www.useragents.me/) is either listing traffic over way too short of a timespan, doesn't get enough traffic, or is receiving an abnormal amount of traffic from somewhere. Most likely at least 2 of these.

Even stranger is that [useragents.me/api](https://www.useragents.me/api) doesn't suffer from these issues but hasn't been updated since the start of this year. It is severely outdated but does correctly put Windows before Mac OS and both Chrome & Firefox before Safari.

You could get a guess out of [useragents.me](https://www.useragents.me/)'s data by limiting it to only the first couple of UAs and then dragging any Safari or Mac OS results to the bottom but that wouldn't be good for anything beyond getting the latest version numbers.

</details>

[jnrbsn/user-agents](https://github.com/jnrbsn/user-agents) fares much better with it scraping [whatismybrowser.com/guides/the-latest-user-agent](https://www.whatismybrowser.com/guides/the-latest-user-agent/) for information but is missing recent history, with latest -1 versions being removed from the list as soon as a new version is out.
